what_its_for: Penicillin V is an antibiotic used to treat bacterial infections such as strep throat, ear infections, skin infections, and dental infections. It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection. Remember, it does NOT work for viral infections like the common cold or flu.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food, but taking it on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after a meal) may help it work better. Always finish ALL of your medication even if you start feeling better — stopping early can cause the infection to come back or become harder to treat.
dosing: Take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed, usually 2 to 4 times a day. Common adult doses range from 250 mg to 500 mg per dose. For children, the dose is based on body weight. Always follow your doctor's or pharmacist's specific instructions, as your dose may be different depending on your infection.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store Penicillin V tablets or capsules at room temperature, away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. If you have the liquid (oral suspension) form, keep it in the refrigerator and shake it well before each use. Throw away any unused liquid after 14 days — do not use it after that time.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids within 2 hours of your dose, as they can reduce how well the medicine works. Do not skip doses or stop taking the antibiotic early, even if you feel better. Tell your doctor if you are on blood thinners like warfarin, as Penicillin V may affect how they work. Avoid this medication if you have a known allergy to penicillin or cephalosporin antibiotics.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek emergency medical help right away if you experience: a skin rash, hives, or itching; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; difficulty breathing or swallowing; severe diarrhea that is watery or bloody; yellowing of the skin or eyes; or if your symptoms are not improving after 3 days of treatment. These may be signs of a serious allergic reaction or another medical problem.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel better within 2 to 3 days of starting Penicillin V. However, it is very important to finish the entire course of antibiotics as prescribed, even if you feel completely well. This ensures the infection is fully cleared and helps prevent antibiotic resistance.
special_populations: Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Penicillin V is generally considered safe during pregnancy and breastfeeding, but always tell your doctor before taking it. Children: The liquid form is available and dosing is based on the child's weight — follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Elderly patients: No special dose adjustments are usually needed, but tell your doctor about all other medications you take. Kidney disease: Let your doctor know if you have kidney problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
